title: Converts to the Order (hedge wizards joining Hermes)
heading: Converts to the Order
requires: Hedge wizard character who swears the Oath of Hermes (House Ex Miscellanea)
summary: How to build a Gifted hedge wizard who has converted to the Order: use the tradition's creation rules up to the Oath, then continue as a Hermetic magus, with limits on learning the Hermetic Arts and social consequences of the conversion.
quotes: Once the character has sworn the Oath of Hermes he gains the free Social Status Virtue Hermetic Magus
related: Houses of Hermes: Societates, House Ex Miscellanea

title: UnGifted Hedge Wizards and the Order
heading: UnGifted Hedge Wizards
requires: unGifted hedge wizard seeking membership in the Order
summary: Explains why membership is normally restricted to Gifted characters, the rare exceptions, and what an unGifted member could never do; includes the sample spell The Numbness of The Gift for sensing the Gift.
quotes: Membership in the Order of Hermes is restricted to characters with The Gift.

title: Identifying The Gift
heading: Identifying The Gift
summary: How Hermetic Intellego Vim effects detect the Gift and hedge Arts or Supernatural Abilities, giving the effective residual magnitude of such a target.
quotes: an effective residual magnitude of his highest Art / 5
effective residual magnitude equal to his highest Supernatural Ability Score

title: Hedge wizards and Certamen
heading: Certamen
requires: Hedge wizard facing a certamen challenge
summary: Hedge wizards cannot take part in certamen unless their Hermetic Arts are Opened; a hedge wizard who accepts a challenge simply loses, which makes converts targets for bullying.
quotes: he cannot cause his phantasm to manifest

title: Allies to the Order (hedge allies of covenants)
heading: Allies to the Order
requires: Covenant or magus allied with a hedge tradition
summary: How to represent hedge-tradition allies of a covenant or a single magus with Covenant Boons and Virtues such as Social Contacts and Personal Vis Source.
quotes: Minor Virtue Social Contacts (ArM5, page 49)

title: Hedge Wizards and the Aegis of the Hearth
heading: Hedge Wizards and the Aegis of the Hearth
requires: Hedge wizard meeting an Aegis of the Hearth
summary: How a hedge wizard's magic interacts with an Aegis of the Hearth: casting towards it must Penetrate, casting inside it suffers a penalty, and tokens or participation grant immunity.
quotes: half the level of the Aegis is subtracted from his Casting Total
related: ArM5 p.161 Aegis of the Hearth

title: Hedge Magic: common rules
heading: Hedge Magic
summary: Introduces the common rules shared by hedge traditions and advises troupes designing their own traditions to break only a few of them.

title: The Gift in hedge traditions
heading: The Gift
summary: Notes that some hedge traditions are exclusively Gifted and others include unGifted members, and what that implies about their size, isolation and survival.

title: Opening the Gift (hedge traditions)
heading: Opening the Gift
summary: A season-long ritual in which a Gifted master Opens an apprentice's Gift to the tradition; if the apprentice already has Supernatural Abilities or Arts, an Opening Total is compared with an Opening Ease Factor, with a worked example.
quotes: It takes one season to Open The Gift, which occupies both the apprentice and the master for the whole season.
**Opening Ease Factor:** twice apprentice's Supernatural Ability + Art scores (+ 12 if Gift already Open)
unless the Opening Total exceeds twice the Opening Ease Factor the apprentice loses his existing Supernatural Ability and Art Scores

title: Flawed Opening of The Gift
heading: Flawed Opening of The Gift
summary: A master who lacks competence in the tradition's Arts and Abilities passes on a Flaw to the apprentice for each shortfall.
quotes: the character must have a score of at least 2 in each Supernatural Ability and Art of the tradition

title: Opening the Arts after a hedge Opening
heading: Opening the Arts
requires: Apprentice whose Gift was already Opened by a hedge tradition
summary: Adds a penalty to the Intellego Vim Lab Total needed to Open the Hermetic Arts of an apprentice whose Gift has already been Opened by a hedge tradition.
quotes: add 30 to the Intellego Vim Lab Total required by the magus

title: Social Penalty of the Gift (hedge traditions)
heading: Social Penalty of the Gift
summary: Gifted hedge wizards suffer the Gift's social penalty even with other Gifted characters unless their tradition has found a remedy comparable to Parma Magica.

title: The Limits of Magic and hedge magic
heading: The Limits of Magic
summary: Hedge magic is bound by the Limits of Magic; troupe-designed traditions should break at most one Lesser Limit and no Greater Limit, and should respect the new Limit of Magic Resistance.
quotes: traditions devised by the troupe break no more than one of the Lesser Limits of Magic

title: Hedge Arts and Supernatural Abilities
heading: Hedge Arts and Supernatural Abilities
summary: Hedge traditions produce effects through combinations of hedge Arts, through Supernatural Abilities, or both; hedge Arts do not combine with Hermetic Arts or with other traditions' Arts.

title: Difficult Arts Mechanically (design guideline)
heading: Difficult Arts Mechanically
summary: Design advice: if a combination of hedge Arts can affect magi, at least one of them should be a Difficult Art so hedge wizards cannot easily get high Penetration.

title: Difficult Arts
heading: Difficult Arts
summary: Difficult Arts are bought and advanced like Abilities rather than Arts, but otherwise act as Arts for vis study, Magical Foci and Virtues that affect Arts.
quotes: it costs 5 experience points for a score of 1, 15 experience points for a score of 2, etc

title: Accelerated Abilities
heading: Accelerated Abilities
summary: The counterpart to Difficult Arts: Abilities that advance like Arts at one experience point for a score of 1, are not capped at creation, and are otherwise treated as Abilities.
quotes: costing one experience point for a score of 1

title: Favored Abilities
heading: Favored Abilities
requires: Gifted member of a tradition with favored Supernatural Abilities
summary: Gifted characters of some traditions need not subtract their favored Supernatural Ability scores from the source quality when learning other favored Abilities, but do subtract all of them when learning non-favored ones.

title: The Limit of Magic Resistance
heading: The Limit of Magic Resistance
summary: A proposed new Limit of Magic: no hedge tradition has a general resistance to magic, and the Order ruthlessly eliminates any that develop one.
quotes: No hedge tradition has a general resistance to magic.

title: Magic Defenses (hedge wizards)
heading: Magic Defenses
requires: Hedge tradition that grants Magical Defenses
summary: Hedge wizards have no true Magic Resistance but may gain limited Magical Defense Bonuses in their area of specialty, derived from a hedge Art or Supernatural Ability; defenses do not stack, cannot be switched off and do not apply to Personal Range effects.
quotes: **Magical Defense Bonus:** Art divided by 5 (round up) or Ability Score
Magical defenses are not cumulative.
Magical defenses do not apply to effects that have a Personal Range.
related: Hedge Magic: Greater Magical Defenses and No Magical Defenses

title: Magical Defense: Accelerated Expiry
heading: Accelerated Expiry
summary: Spells cast on the hedge wizard within his specialty expire early by an amount that depends on the spell's Duration category.
quotes: Diameter Duration spells expire a number of rounds too early equal to the hedge wizard's Magical Defense Bonus, but last at least one round.

title: Magical Defense: Alacritous Fortune
heading: Alacritous Fortune
summary: The hedge wizard adds his Magical Defense Bonus to his Defense Total against spells aimed at him.
quotes: The hedge wizard adds his Magical Defense Bonus to his Defense Total when spells are aimed at him.

title: Magical Defense: Confounding Magics
heading: Confounding Magics
summary: Makes Concentration rolls harder for casters of Concentration-duration effects aimed at the hedge wizard; in a Group effect only the best bonus among such hedge wizards applies.
quotes: Add the hedge wizards Magical Defense Bonus to the Ease Factor of Concentration rolls

title: Magical Defense: Immovable Object
heading: Immovable Object
summary: Each round the hedge wizard rolls to shake off a controlling effect in his specialty, with his Strength and Magical Defense Bonus offsetting the effect's magnitude.
quotes: Strength + Magical Defense Bonus

title: Magical Defense: Magical Fortitude
heading: Magical Fortitude
summary: Damaging effects in the hedge wizard's specialty are soaked with an added Magical Defense Bonus.
quotes: he receives a Magical Defense Bonus to his Soak Total

title: Magical Defense: Strength of Form
heading: Strength of Form
requires: Hedge tradition granting Strength of Form
summary: When a form-changing effect in his specialty affects him, the hedge wizard may roll to return to his natural form.
quotes: Stamina + Magical Defense Bonus + simple die roll against an Ease Factor of 9

title: Warping of hedge wizards
heading: Warping
summary: Hedge wizards gain Warping Points by the usual methods except from living in a strong magic aura, and have no Wizard's Twilight; unGifted ones react like mundane characters and Gifted ones react in tradition-specific ways.
quotes: he does not accumulate Warping points due to living in a strong magic aura

title: Vis and hedge wizards: detecting vis
heading: Vis
summary: Introduces how hedge wizards may use and detect vis, leading into the Magic Sensitivity and non-supernatural detection methods.

title: Detecting vis with Magic Sensitivity
heading: Magic Sensitivity
summary: A character with Magic Sensitivity can tell whether an object holds vis by rolling against an Ease Factor that falls as the vis in it rises.
quotes: make a roll of Perception + Magic Sensitivity against an Ease Factor of (12 — the number of pawns of vis contained in the object)

title: Detecting vis without supernatural means: Perception
heading: Non-supernatural Perception
summary: A character without supernatural senses can pick the objects most likely to hold vis from a collection using Perception and a Theory or Magic Lore Ability; the result is only a guess until the vis is used.
quotes: make a Perception + (Hedge Magic) Theory or Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 12

title: Detecting vis without supernatural means: Intelligence
heading: Non-supernatural Intelligence
summary: A character can reason about where vis is likely to be found (for example, the first fruit of the season) with an Intelligence roll; finding it remains trial and error.
quotes: make a roll for the character of Intelligence + (Hedge Magic) Theory or Magic Lore against an Ease Factor of 15

title: Creating Hedge Characters
heading: Creating Hedge Characters
summary: Introduces the general framework for generating hedge wizard characters that each tradition chapter builds on.

title: Hedge wizard as a Gifted Companion
heading: As a Gifted Companions
summary: A Gifted companion gets The Gift for free, up to a set number of Virtue points balanced by Flaws, and usually gains access to the tradition's whole suite of powers through a free Social Status after Opening The Gift.
quotes: Such a character may have up to 10 points worth of Virtues and balancing Flaws

title: Hedge wizard as an unGifted Companion
heading: As an unGifted Companion
summary: An unGifted hedge wizard buys each power through individual Virtues and has no Gift to Open, so is typically weaker than a Gifted one.
quotes: An un-Gifted companion character may have up to 10 points worth of Virtues and balancing Flaws.

title: Hedge wizard as a Mythic Companion
heading: As a Mythic Companion
summary: A more powerful unGifted hedge wizard built as a Mythic Companion with the free Mythic Companion Status, extra Flaws balancing double their value in Virtues, and an extra Minor Virtue.
quotes: The character also receives an extra Minor Virtue at no cost. This means that the Mythic Companion character has a maximum of 21 points of Virtues.

title: Hedge wizard as a Grog
heading: As a Grog
summary: A very minor unGifted hedge wizard can be a grog with a few Minor Virtues representing his powers.
quotes: created as a grog character who has up to three Minor Virtues to represent his powers

title: Concerns in building hedge characters
heading: Concerns
summary: Reminds troupes to follow the normal Virtue and Flaw mix for each character type, that only Gifted companions may take Hermetic Virtues and Flaws, and how hedge characters compare in power to magi when allocating them to players.
quotes: only Gifted companion characters may be assigned Hermetic Virtues and Flaws

title: Hermetic Virtues and Flaws for hedge wizards
heading: Hermetic Virtues and Flaws
summary: A Gifted hedge wizard may take Hermetic Virtues and Flaws that make sense for his tradition; unGifted members may get Supernatural versions, and may only take a Supernatural Flaw that limits a Virtue he has.
quotes: An unGifted character may only take a Supernatural Flaw of this sort if he has a Virtue that will be limited by it.

title: Free Social Status: (Hedge Wizard)
heading: Free Social Status: (Hedge Wizard)
summary: Each tradition has its own free Social Status Virtue: for Gifted members it reflects the Opening of The Gift and access to favored Abilities or Arts, while unGifted members need the individual Virtues but still gain the social standing.

title: Arcane Abilities of hedge wizards
heading: Arcane Abilities
summary: The hedge wizard Social Status gives access to the Arcane Abilities Finesse, Magic Lore and Penetration, and often a tradition-specific analogue of Magic Theory.
quotes: at least the Arcane Abilities Finesse, Magic Lore, and Penetration

title: (Hedge Magic) Theory
heading: (Hedge Magic) Theory
requires: Hedge tradition with a theoretical basis
summary: An Arcane Ability covering the technical practice of a hedge tradition's magic; traditions without practitioners holding it are poor at innovation, new effects and teaching.

title: (Organization) Lore for hedge traditions
heading: (Organization) Lore
summary: A General Ability for the legends, history, structure and goals of each hedge tradition; membership is not required, and some traditions use it in initiations.

title: Inherited and Learned Powers
heading: Inherited and Learned Powers
summary: Hedge powers are either inherited as Supernatural Virtues that the tradition then trains, or learned through teaching, initiations or Opening the Gift; players should decide how a character acquired his powers.

title: Hedge powers during character generation
heading: During Character Generation
summary: A Gifted companion with an Opened Gift may spend starting experience on tradition Arts and Abilities, while an unGifted one may only do so for those powers for which he has the corresponding Virtues.

title: Hedge powers during play
heading: During Play
summary: In play, hedge wizards improve existing Supernatural Abilities and Arts normally but cannot learn new ones without the necessary Virtues, typically gained by initiation.

title: Hedge tradition Initiations
heading: Initiations
requires: Hedge tradition that teaches powers by Initiation
summary: A Mystagogue directs the Initiate through a Script of mystically significant tasks; an Initiation Total plus Script Bonus is compared to an Ease Factor and, on success, the Initiate gains a power, usually a Virtue.
quotes: If the Mystagogue does not personally know the power then the Ease Factor is increased by 3 (if the power is a Minor Virtue), or by 9 (if the power is a Major Virtue).
The Script Bonus is added to the Initiation Total.

title: UnGifted Initiations
heading: UnGifted Initiations
requires: Hedge tradition that Initiates unGifted characters
summary: Special rules for traditions that initiate unGifted characters: the Initiation must include an Ordeal, earlier Ordeals do not count, and the Initiate cannot act as his own Mystagogue.
quotes: Initiations that affect unGifted characters must include an Ordeal

title: Integration of Hedge Magic
heading: Integration of Hedge Magic
requires: Hermetic magus researching a hedge tradition
summary: Introduces how Hermetic magi, especially Bonisagus Seekers, study hedge traditions to extend Hermetic theory.

title: The Breakthrough (integrating hedge magic)
heading: The Breakthrough
requires: Hermetic magus researching a hedge tradition
summary: Any magus may attempt to integrate a hedge tradition by accumulating breakthrough points; there are Minor, Major and Hermetic Breakthroughs of increasing difficulty, whose exact requirements the storyguide should vary.
quotes: Typically requires around 30 breakthrough points
Typically requires around 45 breakthrough points
Typically requires around 60 breakthrough points
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, original research

title: Insight (integrating hedge magic)
heading: Insight
requires: Hermetic magus researching a hedge tradition
summary: A magus spends seasons studying texts, relics or teachers of a hedge tradition and rolls to gain an insight, which yields Lab Texts and a specified partially Hermetic effect; teachers can also assist.
quotes: make a stress roll of Intelligence + Magic Theory against an Ease Factor of 18
insight Lab Texts have a level equal to the typical number of breakthrough points needed for the type of Breakthrough in question
A teacher can provide a number of insights equal to his (Hedge Magic) Theory Ability, in each Breakthrough associated with his tradition.

title: The Integration Process
heading: The Integration Process
requires: Hermetic magus researching a hedge tradition
summary: A five-step summary: find a source, investigate it for Insight, invent the specified spell or device while experimenting, keep researching to the threshold, then reap the consequences.
quotes: gain a number of breakthrough points equal to the magnitude of the spell or device

title: Creating the Effect (from an insight)
heading: Creating the Effect
summary: An insight fixes one exact effect that the researcher must invent without varying it, gaining breakthrough points equal to its magnitude; other magi can reproduce it only from a Lab Text, again without variation.
quotes: the magus gains a number of breakthrough points equal to the magnitude of the effect
The researcher must invent exactly the effect inspired by the insight.

title: After the Breakthrough
heading: After the Breakthrough
requires: Completed Breakthrough from a hedge tradition
summary: How each kind of Breakthrough spreads: Minor ones are usable at once, Abilities convert breakthrough points to experience, new Virtues are gained without Initiation, and further teaching-free Breakthroughs need another Major Breakthrough.
quotes: so that a magus who accrued 50 breakthrough points to integrate an Ability would start with a score of 4
related: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Initiation Scripts

title: Hermetic Use of Hedge Theory
heading: Hermetic Use of Hedge Theory
requires: Hedge tradition lacking a Theory Ability
summary: A Hermetic researcher or hedge wizard may invent a (Hedge Magic) Theory Ability as a Hermetic Breakthrough, converting the points to experience and then acting as his own source of insight.
quotes: This Breakthrough normally requires 60 breakthrough points, but the researcher reduces this amount by his greatest existing (Hedge Magic) Theory or Magic Theory Ability Score.

title: Original Research and Ancient Magic
heading: Original Research and Ancient Magic
requires: Hermetic magus researching a hedge tradition
summary: Breakthrough points from integrating hedge traditions, original research and ancient traditions are interchangeable for reaching a Breakthrough.
quotes: breakthrough points from integration may be added to breakthrough points from original research to determine whether a Breakthrough has been achieved
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages, original research

title: Integration by Hedge Wizard Researchers
heading: Integration by Hedge Wizard Researchers
requires: Hedge wizard with a (Hedge Magic) Theory Score
summary: Hedge wizards can do their own integration research once they have a Theory Ability, but need more breakthrough points than a Hermetic researcher and face disapproving peers.
quotes: a hedge researcher requires double the number of breakthrough points that an equivalent Hermetic researcher would require

title: Elementalist Characters (Arts, vis use and study)
heading: Elementalist Characters
summary: Elementalist magic uses four Techniques and four Forms that work only in combination and come in Medicinal, Philosophical and Theurgical types; it also covers how elementalists add vis to totals and study their Arts from vis or books.
quotes: receiving a +2 bonus for each pawn of vis that corresponds to the Elementalist Form used in the formula
spend a number of pawns of vis associated with that Form equal to (their score in the Technique / 2), rounded up
related: Hedge Magic: Acquiring Hedge Wizard Powers

title: Elemental Affinities & Character Creation
heading: Elemental Affinities & Character Creation
requires: Tradition: Elementalists (Elemental Magic, Medicine, Philosophiae or Theurgy)
summary: Optional character creation method that approximates these Virtues' free experience by treating them as an Affinity with the related Forms.
quotes: an optional method is to treat the Virtue as an Affinity with the related Forms

title: Other Summoning Arts
heading: Other Summoning Arts
requires: Elementalist who also has infernal Summoning
summary: Distinguishes elementalist (Elemental) Summoning from infernal (Spirit) Summoning, and which of Controlling and Commanding works on elementals, spirits or both.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.87, 114-115

title: Elemental Warping
heading: Elemental Warping
summary: Elementalists gain elemental Personality Traits instead of Virtues and Flaws from Warping; the Traits add to Soak against the matching element, subtract from Recovery against matching humoral illness, and become Personality Flaws or madness as they rise.
quotes: divide the Form by 5 (rounded up), and add this result to the value of the corresponding Trait
You must subtract the value of the Trait from the character's Recovery rolls whenever he is suffering from an illness of the corresponding humor.
Treat Traits of +6 or more as Major Personality Flaws

title: Elemental Traits
heading: Elemental Traits
summary: Describes the four elemental Personality Traits (Choleric, Melancholic, Phlegmatic, Sanguine), the Form and opposed Trait for each, and notes that opposed Traits never cancel out.
quotes: The effects of these Traits on the character's personality never cancel each other out

title: Elementalist Forms
heading: Elementalist Forms
summary: Introduces the four Elementalist Forms and what they can affect depending on the paired Technique type.

title: Elementalist Air
heading: Elementalist Air
summary: A Difficult Art; defines what Medicinal, Philosophical and Theurgical elementalists can affect with air and gives a Soak bonus from the Sanguine Trait against air damage.
quotes: The character adds his Sanguine Trait to his Soak whenever he is damaged by the element of air

title: Elementalist Earth
heading: Elementalist Earth
summary: A Difficult Art; defines what elementalists can affect with earth and gives a Soak bonus from the Melancholy Trait against earth damage.
quotes: The character adds his Melancholy Trait to his Soak whenever he is damaged by the element of earth

title: Elementalist Fire
heading: Elementalist Fire
summary: A Difficult Art; defines what elementalists can affect with fire and gives a Soak bonus from the Choleric Trait against fire damage.
quotes: The character adds his Choleric Trait to his Soak whenever he is damaged by the element of fire

title: Elementalist Water
heading: Elementalist Water
summary: A Difficult Art; defines what elementalists can affect with water and gives a Soak bonus from the Phlegmatic Trait against water damage.
quotes: The character adds his Phlegmatic trait to his Soak when he is damaged by the element of water

title: Elementalist Techniques
heading: Elementalist Techniques
summary: Introduces the four Elementalist Techniques, each tied to a Characteristic, combined with a Form and applied to a Medicinal, Philosophical or Theurgical target.

title: Elementalist Summoning
heading: Summoning
summary: The Summoning roll draws elements or targets to the elementalist at the cost of a long-term Fatigue level; the Total is looked up on a Size/Might chart, multiple Forms use the lowest score, summoning containers hold targets and ease later effects, and botches lose control.
quotes: **SUMMONING TOTAL:** stress die + Stamina + Summoning + (Form) + aura
This procedure always costs the elementalist a long-term Fatigue level

title: Summoning (Medicinal)
heading: Medicinal
summary: An elemental physician touches a target to cure or cause disease by shifting its humors, with the Summoning Total giving the strength of the disease in terms of wound and illness severity.
quotes: one magnitude more affects a disease equivalent to a Medium wound or a serious illness

title: Summoning (Philosophical)
heading: Philosophical
summary: An elemental philosopher conjures raw natural phenomena or base matter, or native animals of a fitting temperament, within the Size and Might limits set by the Summoning Total.
quotes: of an amount no more than the Size indicated by the Summoning Total on the chart earlier

title: Summoning (Theurgical)
heading: Theurgical
summary: An elemental theurgist brings an elemental into being from raw base material, with the Summoning Total setting its maximum Might; the elemental is permanent but cannot recover Might except by consuming vis.
quotes: Elementals are permanently summoned, but do not recover their Might Points over time unless they consume vis

title: Summoning Elementals
heading: Summoning Elementals
summary: Summoned elementals are temporary, revert to base material when their Might Pool is empty, regain Might by eating vis (preferring the opposed Form), and are wild and dangerous unless contained.
quotes: each pawn an elemental consumes returns 5 points of Might to it

title: Elementalist Controlling
heading: Controlling
summary: Controlling lets an elementalist dictate the behavior of summoned or encountered targets; it costs an ordinary Fatigue level, takes a round, must penetrate Magic Resistance, and is much easier against a bound target.
quotes: **CONTROLLING TOTAL:** stress die + Presence + Controlling + (Form) + aura

title: Controlling (Medicinal)
heading: Medicinal
summary: An elemental physician inspires or suppresses emotions as a temporary Personality Trait scaled to the Controlling Total, and can command supernatural creatures lodged in a human body.
quotes: roughly equivalent to a Personality Trait with a positive or negative value of (Controlling Total / 10), rounded up

title: Controlling (Philosophical)
heading: Philosophical
summary: An elemental philosopher can boost his Soak against a material of the matching element and give commands to animals of the matching temperament.
quotes: He may add his (Controlling Total / 5) to his Soak against the target material for as long as he maintains concentration

title: Controlling (Theurgical)
heading: Theurgical
summary: An elemental theurgist who equals or exceeds a being's Might can force it to carry out a single command, or banish an elemental permanently.
quotes: assuming he can equal or exceed the being's Might on his Controlling roll

title: Elementalist Divining
heading: Divining
summary: Divining costs no Fatigue and either senses an appropriate target nearby (Size only) or, by touch, communes with it (Size and Might, and penetration); it can also locate vis of an element and uses the lower Form when several are combined.
quotes: **Divining Total:** stress die + Perception + Divining + (Form) + aura

title: Divining (Medicinal)
heading: Medicinal
summary: An elemental physician diagnoses humoral imbalance and, by tending a patient through recovery, adds a fraction of the Divining Total as magical aid to the patient's recovery roll.
quotes: treat his (Divining Total / 5) as magical aid for the purposes of the target's recovery roll

title: Divining (Philosophical)
heading: Philosophical
summary: An elemental philosopher senses natural materials of an element and animals of the matching temperament, including understanding an animal's thoughts by touch.

title: Divining (Theurgical)
heading: Theurgical
summary: An elemental theurgist senses beings with Might of the element in the region and can converse with them or perceive their past by touch.

title: Elementalist Refining
heading: Refining
summary: A season-long laboratory-like activity that purifies or breaks down a target, often yielding raw vis; it also lets an elementalist brew a longevity potion costing vis scaled to his age.
quotes: **REFINING TOTAL:** Intelligence + (associated Ability) + Refining + (Form) + aura
The potion gives him a bonus to his Aging rolls equal to his (Refining Total /5)
costs a number of pawns of vis equal to his (age /5), rounded up

title: Refining (Medicinal)
heading: Medicinal
summary: An elemental physician can make longevity potions for others and a year-long vigor potion that boosts a Characteristic chosen by Element, capped by his lowest Form; a table lists the Characteristics per element.
quotes: This boosts one of the target's Characteristics (as shown below) by the elementalist's (Refining Total / 5)

title: Refining (Philosophical)
heading: Philosophical
summary: An elemental philosopher extracts vis from an aura, drains or boosts the Might of supernatural animals for vis, and moves vis between objects, losing half if the Form must be changed.
quotes: producing his (Refining Total / 10) in vis associated with the appropriate one of the four elements
his Refining Total for the season must equal or exceed (the total number of pawns of vis moved x 5)

title: Refining (Theurgical)
heading: Theurgical
summary: An elemental theurgist restores Might to, or drains it from, an elemental or supernatural being depending on whether the Form matches, opposes or is unrelated to its own, producing vis from surplus or lost Might.
quotes: this is the number of Might Points restored to it

title: Elementalist Societies (and Opening the Gift)
heading: Elementalist Societies
summary: Societies teach particular Techniques and Forms; a Gifted member opens a Gifted student's Gift using a specific Opening Total, and the society's Arts indicate what unGifted initiates can be taught.
quotes: **OPENING TOTAL:** Intelligence + highest Technique + lowest Form + aura

title: Apostles of Apollonius
heading: Apostles of Apollonius
summary: An elementalist society that favors (Theurgical) Summoning, (Theurgical) Controlling and all four Elementalist Forms, with history and notes on its distribution in 1220.

title: Ikhwan as-Safa' (Brethren of Purity)
heading: Ikhwan as-Safa'
summary: An elementalist society whose Arts are Philosophical Summoning, Philosophical Refining and all four Elementalist Forms.

title: Teaching of the Brethren of Purity (grades)
heading: Teaching of the Brethern of Purity
summary: The Brethren advance through four grades with minimum Ability scores; Gifted members learn the society's Arts directly while unGifted members must be initiated.

title: Bload Oath of Becoming a Member of Ikhwan as-Safa'
heading: Bload Oath of Becoming a Member of Ikhwan as-Safa'
summary: Initiation Script that grants the Major Virtue Philosophical Refining with the Major Flaw Weak Elementalist Resistance, after a quest, a tractatus and a season of study.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 21
**Script Bonus:** +18 (+3 Quest, +9 Major Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sacrifice, +1 Sympathetic Bonus)

title: Ritual of Uncovering the Elemental Nature of Man
heading: Ritual of Uncovering the Elemental Nature of Man
summary: Initiation Script that grants a score of 1 in an Elementalist Form (chosen by the Initiate's temperament) plus the Minor Flaw Mentor.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 15
**Script Bonus:** +12 (+3 Quest, +3 Minor Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sympathetic Bonus, +1 Sacrifice)

title: Ritual of Making the Soul Actually Knowledgeable
heading: Ritual of Making the Soul Actually Knowledgeable
summary: Initiation Script that grants the Major Virtue Elemental Philosophiae and the Major Flaw Study Requirement after the supplicant writes a summa.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 21
**Script Bonus:** +18 (+3 Quest, +9 Major Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sacrifice, +1 Sympathetic Bonus)

title: Ikhwan as-Safa' Characters
heading: Characters
summary: Character generation notes for Brethren: yearly experience points for Arcane and Academic Abilities, typical Abilities, Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: they receive 30 experience points to spend on Arcane and Academic Abilities
related: Learned Magicians: Mythic Alchemy, Mythic Herbalism

title: Tulab Ibn Sina
heading: Tulab Ibn Sina
summary: An elementalist society of Islamic physicians whose Arts are Medicinal Summoning, Medicinal Divining and all four Elementalist Forms.

title: Teachings of Ibn Sina (access to Arts)
heading: Teachings of Ibn Sina
summary: Who the Tulab accept as students; Gifted members learn Medicinal Summoning, Medicinal Divining and the Forms, while unGifted members gain Arts only through Initiation.
quotes: Gifted members of this tradition learn Medicinal Summoning, Medicinal Divining, and all the Elementalist Forms.

title: Rite of Testing the Physician's Dedication
heading: Rite of Testing the Physician's Dedication
summary: Initiation Script granting a score of 1 in Medicinal Divining and the Major Flaw Restriction after a year of aiding disaster victims.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 21
**Script Bonus:** +18 (+3 Quest, +9 Major Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +2 Sympathetic Bonus)

title: Ritual of Discovering the Physician's Humor
heading: Ritual of Discovering the Physician's Humor
summary: Initiation Script in which the supplicant recovers from a Medium Wound as a pauper, then gains a score of 1 in an Elementalist Form matching his humor and the Minor Flaw Vow.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 15
**Script Bonus:** +11 (+3 Quest, +3 Minor Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sympathetic Bonus)

title: Ritual of Improving the Physician's Character
heading: Ritual of Improving the Physician's Character
summary: Initiation Script granting the Major Virtue Elemental Medicine and the Major Flaw Study Requirement after a year of free healing for the poor.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 21
**Script Bonus:** +18 (+3 Quest, +9 Major Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +1 Sympathetic Bonus, +1 Sacrifice)

title: Rite of Opening the Mind
heading: Rite of Opening the Mind
summary: Initiation Script involving a season of fasting and prayer at Ibn Sina's tomb, with a Stamina roll, granting a score of 1 in Premonitions with the Flaw Visions.
quotes: **Initiation Ease Factor:** 15
**Script Bonus:** +12 (+3 Quest, +3 Minor Ordeal, +3 Mystagogue's Time, +1 Initiate's Time, +2 Sympathetic Bonus)
the player makes a Stamina roll against an Ease Factor of 9

title: Tulab Ibn Sina Characters
heading: Characters
summary: Character generation notes for Tulab members: a short intense training period with set experience points, favored Abilities, typical Virtues and Flaws, and the Educated Virtue's allocation for Islamic lands.
quotes: In a five-year period, the student gains 150 experience points to spend on Academic and Arcane Abilities.
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.101, 114

title: Hermetic Integration of Elementalist magic
heading: Hermetic Integration
summary: Minor Breakthroughs convert Elementalist background Virtues into Hermetic ones; a Major Breakthrough lets a magus substitute a Hermetic Technique or Form for an adapted Elementalist Art.
quotes: a magus may substitute his score in an appropriate Hermetic Technique or Form for his score in the Elementalist Art
related: Hedge Magic: Integration of Hedge Magic

title: Creating a Folk Witch Character
heading: Creating a Folk Witch Character
summary: Folk witches may be Gifted or unGifted (companion or grog), need at least one Flaw limiting their magic and the free Folk Witch Status, spend a ten-year apprenticeship with a special experience allotment, and can do limited laboratory work during creation.
quotes: you may spend 200 experience points for the character on any Abilities
which gives her seven favored Supernatural Abilities
Each season spent on laboratory activities reduce the number of experience points received for that year by 10

title: Folk Witch minimum Ability Scores
heading: Minimum Ability Scores
summary: Minimum Ability scores expected of a Gifted folk witch after apprenticeship, and the language scores needed for a literate or writing witch.
quotes: she must have a score of at least 4 in a Language (which does not need to be Latin), and a score of at least 1 in Artes Liberales

title: Folk Witch (Social Status)
heading: Folk Witch
summary: The free Social Status that grants folk witch laboratory activities, casting methods and magical defenses, coven membership and sabbat attendance, and requires two seasons a year of self-support.
quotes: she must spend two seasons each year supporting herself

title: Folk Witch Magic
heading: Folk Witch Magic
summary: Folk witches use seven favored Supernatural Abilities, advanced on the standard Ability table, accessed by potions, incantations or fetish objects, with limited Magical Defenses but no Magic Resistance.
quotes: folk witches use the standard Ability experience advancement table when improving these Abilities

title: Folk Witch Powers (casting formulas)
heading: Folk Witch Powers
summary: A folk witch's Casting Score is a Characteristic plus Ability plus aura, plus a stress die for the Total, compared to the effect's Ease Factor; Gifted witches can add vis, and Penetration follows from the Total.
quotes: **FOLK WITCH CASTING SCORE:** Characteristic + Ability + Aura Modifier
**MAGNITUDE OF EFFECT:** Ability
**EQUIVALENT SPELL LEVEL:** (5 x Ability)
**PENETRATION TOTAL:** Casting Total + Penetration Bonus — Ease Factor
**MAXIMUM VIS EXPENDITURE:** Ability + Effect Vis Cost

title: Folk Witch Casting Methods
heading: Casting Methods
summary: Each Ability must be used by Potion, Incantation (a rhyme the target hears) or Fetish (a prepared item), with rules for losing the incantation from memory and for spare fetishes.
quotes: make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 6 for her every day after the memory-altering effect ceases

title: Folk Witch Botches
heading: Botches
summary: A botch makes the effect happen uncontrolled and gives the witch Warping Points.
quotes: She also gains 1 Warping Point for every 0 on the botch dice

title: Folk Witch Mark
heading: Mark
summary: Each witch's effects carry a personal mark that others can recognize with a Perception and Organization Lore roll; identifying merely that a witch cast it is easier.
quotes: make a Perception + Organization Lore: Folk Witch roll against an Ease Factor of 9
a successful Perception + Organization Lore: Folk Witch roll against an Ease Factor of 6 identifies an effect as one cast by a Folk Witch

title: Folk Witch Ability: Animal Ken
heading: Animal Ken
summary: Folk witch Animal Ken uses Communication and the Animal Form, delivered by incantation or potion.
quotes: Characteristic: Communication

title: Folk Witch Ability: Cursing (and the curses)
heading: Cursing
summary: A witch curses a target via a woven fetish or potion, using Dexterity and a Form that depends on the curse; each curse type (disease, miscarriage, aging, emotion, tongue, paralysis, beast, reduction) has its own Ease Factor and effect, and the curse must penetrate the target's Magic Resistance throughout the preparation season.
quotes: Preparing the curse is a laboratory activity that takes the folk witch an entire season
use the highest Magic Resistance the target has during the season

title: Folk Witch Ability: Dowsing
heading: Dowsing
summary: Folk witch Dowsing uses Perception, a Form that depends on the target, and a fetish or potion; it lets witches find vis.
quotes: This ability is important for folk witches as it allows them to find vis.

title: Folk Witch Ability: Flight
heading: Flight
summary: A witch can fly using Stamina and Auram, at the cost of a long-term Fatigue level when using a fetish; it describes speed, duration, maneuver rolls and a combat bonus against non-flying opponents.
quotes: The Ease Factor to take to the air is 9.
her Flight Ability score is added to both her Attack and Defense Totals

title: Folk Witch Ability: Healing
heading: Healing
summary: True healing of wounds and Fatigue that breaks the Limit of Energy; it costs Corpus vis according to a table of Ease Factors by wound or fatigue level, and must penetrate the target's Magic Resistance.
quotes: the folk witch must spend a number of pawns of Corpus vis depending on the wound type (indicated below)

title: Folk Witch Ability: Second Sight
heading: Second Sight
summary: Folk witch Second Sight uses Perception and the Vim Form, delivered by incantation or potion.
quotes: Form: Vim

title: Folk Witch Ability: Shapeshifter
heading: Shapeshifter
summary: Folk witch Shapeshifter uses Stamina and the Animal Form, delivered by fetish (made from the animal's skin) or potion.
quotes: The fetish is made from the skin of the animal form.

title: Folk Witch Magical Defenses
heading: Magical Defenses
summary: Lists which Magical Defense each folk witch power grants (for example Healing gives Magical Fortitude against Corpus effects); an unGifted witch only gets defenses for powers she has.
quotes: Defense: Strength of Form. Defense against Animal or Corpus effects.

title: Witch's Kitchen
heading: Witch's Kitchen
summary: A folk witch's kitchen works like a laboratory, with a Lab Total built from a Supernatural Ability, Intelligence, Folk Witch Magic Theory and aura; unGifted witches may do tasks only if they hold the matching Virtues.
quotes: **Lab Total:** (Supernatural Ability) + Intelligence + Folk Witch Magic Theory + Aura Modifier

title: Folk Witch Magic Theory
heading: Folk Witch Magic Theory
summary: An Arcane Ability analogous to Magic Theory, covering the technical details of folk witch magic and used in kitchen laboratory activities; any character can be taught it.
quotes: Any character can be taught this Ability.

title: Building the Kitchen
heading: Building the Kitchen
summary: Setting up a witch's kitchen or converting a Hermetic laboratory takes set seasons and minimum Theory scores; Covenants laboratory rules can be used with a size-scale adjustment.
quotes: **SETTING UP A KITCHEN:** 2 Seasons and a minimum Folk Witch Magic Theory score of 3
add 3 to the Laboratory Size Scale

title: Help in the Kitchen
heading: Help in the Kitchen
summary: Folk witches work alone except for their familiar and for mutual aid at a sabbat.

title: Experimenting (folk witches)
heading: Experimenting
summary: Folk witches experiment as Hermetic magi do, gaining a Lab Total bonus and rolling on the Extraordinary Results table, often to overcome Divine aura penalties.
quotes: **EXPERIMENTAL BONUS TO LAB TOTAL:** Simple die + Risk Modifier

title: Folk Witch Lab Texts
heading: Lab Texts
summary: Only literate witches can write or use Lab Texts, which follow the Hermetic copying and writing rules but are not useful to magi and vice versa.

title: Folk Witch Vis (extraction, transfer, use)
heading: Vis
summary: Witches find vis by Dowsing, extract Vim vis from the aura each season based on their Lab Total, move vis between forms in a day, and may use only a limited amount in laboratory projects.
quotes: extract a number of pawns of Vim vis from the local aura equal to a tenth of her Lab Total (round up)
can only use up to twice her Folk Witch Magic Theory Ability score in pawns of vis on laboratory projects

title: Fixing Arcane Connections
heading: Fixing Arcane Connections
summary: In a season a witch can lengthen an Arcane Connection's lifetime by one step, using her Lab Total and a pawn of Vim vis.
quotes: costs 1 pawn of Vim vis

title: Folk Witch Study
heading: Study
summary: Studying in the kitchen gives no bonus, and learning Supernatural Abilities remains difficult or impossible for unGifted witches without an existing score.

title: Curse Fetish Weaving
heading: Curse Fetish Weaving
summary: Weaving a curse fetish occupies a season in a kitchen, needs an active Arcane Connection to the target, and some curses take effect at once while others last until the fabric is destroyed or the connection expires.
quotes: creating a single fabric (which targets an Individual) both occupies the character for an entire season, and requires a kitchen

title: Dowsing Rod Binding
heading: Dowsing Rod Binding
summary: Enchanting a dowsing rod fetish takes a season and a pawn of Intellego vis, and it lasts indefinitely unless destroyed.
quotes: enchanting a dowsing rod takes 1 season and consumes 1 pawn of Intellego vis

title: Flight Broom Preparation
heading: Flight Broom Preparation
summary: Enchanting a flying aid fetish takes a season and a pawn of Auram vis, and it lasts indefinitely unless destroyed.
quotes: enchanting a flying aid takes 1 season and consumes 1 pawn of Auram vis

title: Skin Knitting
heading: Skin Knitting
summary: Enchanting an animal-skin fetish takes a season and a pawn of Animal vis; a witch needs a separate fetish for each animal type she can take.
quotes: enchanting the fetish takes a season and consumes 1 pawn of Animal vis

title: Potion Brewing
heading: Potion Brewing
summary: A season of brewing yields a batch of doses sharing a Brew Potency equal to the witch's Lab Total; a drinker's effective Casting Total is that Potency plus a stress die, with vis costs per dose and optional Lab Text bonus doses, with a worked example.
quotes: **Brew Potency:** Supernatural Ability Lab Total
**POTION CASTING TOTAL:** Brew Potency + stress die
**Doses per Brew:** Folk Witch Magic Theory (+ Lab Text Level)
**Vis Cost:** 1 per Dose + Effect Cost

title: Potion Effects
heading: Potion Effects
summary: What each Ability's potion does for the drinker: temporary Ability scores and durations derived from the Brew Potency, curse potions, healing potions and shapeshifting.
quotes: with an Ability score equal to the Brew Potency / 5 (round up)

title: Enriching Things of Virtue
heading: Enriching Things of Virtue
summary: A folk witch may enrich Things of Virtue using the rules in Realms of Power: Magic.
related: Realms of Power: Magic, Things of Virtue

title: Folk Witch Longevity Ritual
heading: Longevity Ritual
summary: A witch can make a Longevity Ritual only for herself, using the Hermetic rules with her Healing Lab Total, so it is weaker than a magus's.
quotes: Use her Healing Ability Lab Total for this activity

title: Investigating a Potion
heading: Investigating a Potion
requires: Tradition: Folk Witches or magus familiar with folk witch magic
summary: A witch identifies a potion's Potency and effect with an Intelligence and Theory roll; to a magus a potion is an effect whose detection depends on extra magnitudes of Intellego Vim.
quotes: **POTION INVESTIGATION:** Intelligence + Folk Witch Magic Theory + Stress Die vs Ease Factor of 9

title: Folk Witch Familiars
heading: Familiars
summary: A witch binds one animal as a familiar in a season of laboratory work by beating a Binding Total built from the familiar's Size and Might.
quotes: **FOLK WITCH FAMILIAR BINDING TOTAL:** 10 + Familiar's Size + Familiar's Magic Might
related: Realms of Power: Magic, Book of Mundane Beasts
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.38

title: Benefits of a Folk Witch Familiar
heading: Benefits of a Familiar
summary: A familiar gains human Intelligence and languages, can assist in the kitchen for a Lab Total bonus, ages with its mistress, serves as an Arcane Connection both ways, and lets the witch dowse for it and see through its senses.
quotes: **Familiar Bonus to Lab Total:** Familiar's Intelligence + Familiar's Folk Witch Magic Theory

title: Folk Witch Warping
heading: Warping
summary: Folk witches gain Warping Points as usual plus from botches, but not from Magic auras; each time the Warping Score rises she suffers the Witch Moon instead of Twilight.
quotes: She also gains Warping points when she botches using her Supernatural Abilities.

title: The Witch Moon
heading: The Witch Moon
summary: The folk witch's equivalent of Wizard's Twilight: a month or more of lost Supernatural Abilities and a fever Medium Wound, with a monthly roll to end it and extra Warping Points on failure or botch.
quotes: **TO END WITCH MOON:** Stamina – Warping Score + stress die vs Ease Factor 6

title: Effects of the Witch Moon
heading: Effects of the Witch Moon
summary: After recovering, the witch's experience is good or bad depending on whether the months taken exceeded her Warping Score, and the storyguide picks an effect from the matching list.
quotes: If the folk witch took more months to recover from the Witch Moon than her Warping score, then the experience is bad.

title: Witch Moon: Good Experiences
heading: Good Experiences
summary: Good Witch Moon outcomes: experience points in an existing Ability or Theory, a new Minor Virtue, or a new Supernatural Ability at score 1.
quotes: equal to 5 x number of months spent in the Witch Moon

title: Witch Moon: Bad Experiences
heading: Bad Experinces
summary: Bad Witch Moon outcomes: lost experience in a Supernatural Ability or Theory per Warping Point gained, or a new Minor Flaw.
quotes: She loses 2 experience points in a Supernatural Ability or in Folk Witch Magic Theory for every Warping Point gained during the Witch Moon.

title: Covens
heading: Covens
summary: A coven is the folk witch equivalent of a covenant: a small, dispersed group of witches, each living a day's travel apart, with its strengths and vulnerabilities.

title: Folk Witch Opening the Gift
heading: Opening the Gift
summary: Opening a folk witch's Gift follows the general rules with a folk-witch Opening Total and grants seven favored Supernatural Abilities, which troupes can swap for others.
quotes: **FOLK WITCH OPENING TOTAL:** Int + Folk Witch Magic Theory + Sabbat Bonus

title: Organization Lore: Folk Witches
heading: Organization Lore: Folk Witches
summary: The Ability covers folk witch effects, coven locations and reputations; its specialty is a home coven, with extra botch dice for covens farther away.
quotes: roll an additional botch die for every week's travel this coven is from the character's "home" coven

title: Initiations for unGifted Folk Witches
heading: Initiations for unGifted Folk Witches
summary: unGifted witches are initiated by a Mystagogue who must know the power, with an Initiation Total using Presence and Theory; seven sample Scripts (Rhyme of the Beast, Venomous Darts, Sense of Place, Unbound by Land, Hands of Life, The Devil's Eye, Second Life) give the Supernatural Virtues and their ordeal Flaws.
quotes: **FOLK WITCH INITIATION TOTAL:** Mystagogue's Presence + Mystagogue's Folk Witch Magic Theory + Script Bonus + Sabbat Bonus
**Script Bonus:** +10 (+9 Major Ordeal, +1 Time)

title: Precocious Girls
heading: Precocious Girls
summary: What a coven can do when it accidentally initiates a Gifted girl as if unGifted: find someone to Open her Gift properly or teach her Abilities without favored status.

title: Sabbat
heading: Sabbat
summary: The coven meeting where witches trade vis and discuss threats; because witches lack Parma Magica the Gift's social effects often cause bickering, and a sabbat does not interrupt long-term tasks.

title: Sabbat Politics
heading: Sabbat Politics
summary: Four optional ways a sabbat can run (Easy, Bickering, Dictatorial, Feuding), depending on the Gifted makeup of the coven and the kind of stories wanted.

title: Sabbat Magic
heading: Sabbat Magic
summary: Witches cooperate at a sabbat to raise a brew's Potency, an Opening Total or an Initiation Total by a bonus per assistant limited by the site's Magic aura; each witch may take part in only one activity per sabbat.
quotes: **POTENCY BONUS FOR SABBAT BREW:** +1 each folk witch assisting main caster
**MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ASSISTANTS:** Magic Aura at sabbat site
**TOTAL BONUS FOR SABBAT INITIATION:** +1 each folk witch assisting Mystagogue

title: Sabbat Times
heading: Sabbat Times
summary: A table of the traditional dates on which covens hold sabbats, grouped under the winter and summer solstices.

title: Creating a Coven
heading: Creating a Coven
requires: Saga set in a folk witch coven
summary: A coven can be built with the Customized Covenant Creation rules, either as the saga's focus or as an antagonist, following a few adjustments.

title: Guidelines for a Coven
heading: Guidelines for a Coven
requires: Saga set in a folk witch coven
summary: Covenant creation adjustments for dispersed covens: separate auras per site, Hooks and Boons balanced over the whole coven, vis sources assigned to individuals, initiation scripts bought with Build Points equal to their bonus, and Build Point ranges by power level.
quotes: By default, the coven has a single site with a level-3 aura
Each initiation script costs a number of Build Points equal to the script bonus.

title: Hermetic Integration of folk witch magic
heading: Hermetic Integration
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: Introduces example breakthroughs (Subtle Opening, Energy Magic, Sense of the Mystic, Ritual Items) that can be researched from folk witch practices, left to the troupe to allow or adapt.
quotes: It's up to the troupe to decide if any of them are actually possible in your saga.
related: Hedge Magic: Integration of Hedge Magic

title: Breakthrough: Subtle Opening
heading: Subtle Opening
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: A breakthrough that merges the folk witch Opening of the Gift into the Hermetic Opening of the Arts, so apprentices avoid the Arts penalty when learning Supernatural Abilities; the discoverer may write a Lab Text for it.
quotes: **Suggested Breakthrough Points:** 30
the apprentice gains the Minor Hermetic Virtue: Subtle Opening

title: Subtle Opening: Integration Effects
heading: Integration Effects
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: How Insights contribute to the Subtle Opening: Vim effects, or varying the technique when Opening an apprentice's Arts with an Extraordinary Results roll, with dangers to the apprentice's Gift.
quotes: the magus earns 5 breakthrough points

title: Breakthrough: Energy Magic
heading: Energy Magic
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: Folk witches are not bound by the Limit of Energy, so studying them can yield additional Creo Corpus and Perdo Corpus guidelines for Fatigue.
quotes: Suggested Breakthrough Points: 55

title: New Perdo Corpus Guidelines (Energy Magic)
heading: New Perdo Corpus Guidelines
summary: Guidelines for lengthening Short-Term Fatigue recovery, causing loss of Short-Term or Long-Term Fatigue, and preventing recovery by rest.
quotes: Level 5: Cause a target to lose a Short-Term Fatigue level.

title: New Creo Corpus Guidelines (Energy Magic)
heading: New Creo Corpus Guidelines
summary: Guidelines for speeding Fatigue recovery and restoring Short-Term or Long-Term Fatigue levels; only Momentary Ritual effects truly restore, while other Durations cause the levels to return as Long-Term Fatigue loss.
quotes: Ritual spells formulated according to these guidelines with Momentary Duration truly restore Fatigue levels.
Level 15: Restore a lost Long-Term Fatigue level.

title: Breakthrough: Sense of the Mystic
heading: Sense of the Mystic
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: Studying the folk witch Second Sight, which senses invisible creatures without penetrating their Magic Resistance, yields a new Hermetic Virtue improving Intellego sensing magic; any character with Second Sight can provide insight.
quotes: **Suggested Breakthrough Points:** 45

title: Breakthrough: Ritual Items
heading: Ritual Items
requires: Hermetic magus integrating folk witch magic
summary: Integrating potion brewing could let magi make charged items that hold ritual effects, which is particularly powerful together with Energy Magic.
quotes: **Suggested Breakthrough Points:** 45

title: Ritual Items (charged items with ritual effects)
heading: New Virtue: Ritual Items
summary: Explains how charged items holding ritual effects work: each charge costs the vis the ritual would normally cost, with the usual seasonal vis limit and charge calculation.
quotes: Each charge requires the same number of pawns of vis that casting the effect normally would otherwise cost.
related: ArM5 p.133 Curse of the Unportended Plague
